links.comparator_used: GPT-4o/GPT-4 without retrieval (training knowledge alone), and fine-tuning on variant annotation data
links.outcome: Accuracy of variant annotation and interpretation; factual knowledge injection (data volume, accuracy, cost-effectiveness)
links.effect: RAG integrated 190 million variant annotations into GPT-4o and gave accurate annotations; RAG outperformed fine-tuning in factual knowledge injection in terms of data volume, accuracy, and cost-effectiveness (no numeric accuracy figures in the abstract)
links.quote: Our project also revealed that RAG outperforms fine-tuning in factual knowledge injection in terms of data volume, accuracy, and cost-effectiveness.

links.comparator_used: Off-the-shelf GPT-4 without fine-tuning, and RAG as an alternative way to inject knowledge
links.outcome: Model performance on variant annotation fields
links.effect: Fine-tuning GPT-4 improved performance in some annotation fields, but accuracy across more fields remained suboptimal; RAG outperformed fine-tuning for factual knowledge injection
links.tradeoff: Fine-tuning was less cost-effective and handled less data volume than RAG; accuracy across many fields remained suboptimal
links.quote: Additionally, fine-tuning GPT-4 on variant annotation data also improved model performance in some annotation fields, although the accuracy across more fields remains suboptimal.

design_hint: retrieval grounding (RAG) added to an existing LLM, compared with fine-tuning
